findings.element: interaction-check.mjs:1005-1014, the check named "the error state claims no reading it does not hold"
findings.problem:
The assertion's whole predicate is `!/Last good reading/.test(text)`. The string "Last good reading" appears nowhere in lately.html or fixture.js — grepped both, zero hits; the only occurrence in the repository is inside the assertion itself. It therefore cannot fail. Two further reasons it cannot catch the defect it guards: it scopes `text` to `document.querySelector("main")`, while the reading stamp lives in `
` outside `main`, so it never looks where the stamp is; and it computes `instances` (a real count of readingLong occurrences) and passes it only into the detail string, never into the predicate. I reproduced the exact defect it names: driven at ?state=error&v=light&motion=settled at 1440x960, I appended `

Last reading: 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026. 31 jobs finished in the four weeks to then.

` into the error card. `instances` went 0 -> 1, `claimsLastGood` stayed false, and the assertion still passed. r1's closed finding error-state-invents-a-last-good-reading is currently guarded by nothing.
findings.consequence: A closed finding that no assertion can fail on is an untested claim (L-05, L-06). The error state is the one screen where a fabricated magnitude does the most damage — a reader who is told Tasks did not answer, then shown a figure, has no way to know the figure is stale. That defect can be reintroduced by any future edit and every gate stays green.
findings.fix: Replace the phrase-grep with a positive statement of the policy, measured over the whole document rather than `main`. In state=error, assert that the error card (`main`) contains no digit at all (it currently contains zero: its text is "Tasks did not answer / This reading needs the Tasks records and they did not come back. Nothing below is shown, because a part of this screen would be guessing. / Try again"), and that none of `LATELY_FIXTURE.readingLong`, `readingShort`, the last-four total (31) or the open count (9) appears anywhere inside `main`. Delete the `Last good reading` regex. Before landing it, break it — inject a magnitude into the error card and watch the assertion fail — then restore.
findings.assertion: In state=error at both grounds and all four declared viewports: `document.querySelector('main').textContent` matches no /\d/, and contains none of LATELY_FIXTURE.readingLong, LATELY_FIXTURE.readingShort, String(sum(weeks.slice(8).map(w=>w.v))) or String(bound.openCount). Prove it fails by appending a paragraph containing readingLong to `.center` before restoring.

findings.problem: The solo treatment narrows the plot (`.plot.solo .cols { width: 57px }`) and, since r2, the ruler under it (`.plot.solo ~ .xaxis { width: 57px }`) — but it stops there. The grid track is still `1fr` and the card is still the full page width, so the single 57px mark sits in a reserved chart track and the rest is blank paper. Measured, ?state=first-run&motion=settled: 1440 — card 1084px, chart track 686px, mark 57px, 629px blank to the right of the mark, 58.0% of the card. 1280 — identical, 629px, 58.0%. 768 — card 616px, 509px blank, 82.6%. 390 — card 342px, 251px blank, 73.4%. The hero card is the first object a new owner ever sees on this surface and at every width its dominant feature is empty paper.
findings.consequence: A first-time venue owner meets this card before any other. Two thirds of it is blank, so it reads as a chart that failed to render rather than as a product saying "one week of record so far". It teaches, at first contact, that this screen is unreliable — and the sentence that would explain the blank ("Four weeks of records make a comparison worth printing. Yours arrive on 10 August 2026.") is stacked at the far left, 500px from the mark it is explaining.
findings.fix: Carry the r1/r2 narrowing up one container. Add `.hero:has(.plot.solo) { grid-template-columns: minmax(220px, 300px) auto; }` so the chart track is its content, and `.card.hero:has(.plot.solo) { width: max-content; max-width: 100%; }` so the card ends a rung past its mark instead of at the page edge. Below 900 the hero already stacks; add `.hero:has(.plot.solo) .chart { align-self: start; }` so the mark and its ruler sit under the figure rather than adrift in a full-width track. Nothing new is drawn and no ghost slots are introduced — the container simply stops promising eleven weeks it has already, correctly, refused to draw.
findings.assertion: In state=first-run at every declared viewport and both grounds: the horizontal distance from the right edge of `.plot.solo .cols` to the right edge of `.card.hero` is at most 2 * --gap-room (48px), and no more than 25% of the hero card's width lies to the right of the last drawn mark or text run.

findings.element: .gridline b at bottom:100% and .bar-val in the twelve-week chart, states full / partial / quiet
findings.problem: `max = Math.max(D.peak, D.bestPrior)` and the top gridline prints `Math.round(max * 1)`. Whenever the live partial week is the peak — which it is in the shipping fixture, 12 against a best prior of 8 — the top gridline's value IS the live week's value, and the two labels print side by side at the same height. Measured at 1440, 1280, 768 and 390, all identical: `.bar-val` reads "12 so far", the top `.gridline b` reads "12", the horizontal gap between them is 14.8px and their boxes overlap vertically by 8px. On screen it reads as one string, "12 SO FAR 12", in two colours, at the same 11px tracked mono rank, meaning two different kinds of thing — one a datum, one a scale ceiling. 14.8px is not a rung on the declared ladder either. The source already states the principle it is breaking here, in the comment on the solo plot: "a gridline derived from a single datum labels the datum with itself".
findings.consequence: The owner's eye lands on the top right of the chart — where the live week is — and reads the same number twice, fifteen pixels apart, in two inks. They have to work out whether these are two facts or one, and the top gridline, the only magnitude reference for the eleven finished columns, carries no information the indigo tag has not already given. Twice-named information in the surface's primary figure.
findings.fix: In `chart()`, suppress the top gridline's `` when its value equals the live week's printed value: build the grid as `[0.5, 1].map(g => { const v = Math.round(max * g); const dup = g === 1 && v === D.weeks[D.weeks.length - 1].v; return `${dup ? "" : `${v}`}`; })`. The rule still draws; the numeral is stated once, by the mark that owns it. When the peak is a finished week the top gridline keeps its label exactly as now.
findings.assertion: In states full, partial and quiet at every declared viewport and both grounds: no two elements among `.plot .gridline b`, `.plot .record-tag` and `.plot .bar-val` render the same numeric token, and no two of them have box centres within 24px of each other horizontally while their boxes overlap vertically.

findings.element: .band-head .t-label above the KPI row, and .kpi.lead .sr, in ?state=partial
findings.problem: Driven at ?state=partial: the band head reads "All five counted out of 9" and the lead card speaks "Every card in this row is counted out of these 9 open jobs." Forty pixels below, the due-date card prints an em dash, the words "Not available", and no meter. Measured from the DOM: 5 cards, 3 carrying a meter, 1 unavailable. Four cards are counted out of nine; the header says five, twice — once in ink and once in the accessibility tree. This is the self-contradicting-counts class from the paid defect library ("a header saying 5 of 32 done above a tray labelled 9"), and it is the one place on the surface where the honest-degradation contract is not honoured: everywhere else the missing source resolves to unavailable, here the summary above it quietly counts it.
findings.consequence: The owner reads a header asserting a shared denominator, then a card that says it has no reading. They must decide which to believe about the card they cannot see a number for — is the missing due-date count included in the nine or not? The protected shared-denominator claim is the thing that makes the row's meters comparable, and in the one state where it is untrue the screen still asserts it.
findings.fix: Derive the label from the row rather than typing it. In `movementTwo`, compute `const counted = 4 - (partial ? 1 : 0)` and print `${counted === 4 ? "All five" : "Four of five"} counted out of ${D.open}` — in partial: "Four of five counted out of 9". In `leadKpi`, take the same flag and speak "Every card in this row that could be read is counted out of these 9 open jobs; the due-date card was not read." when a source is unavailable. Both stay one sentence and the shared denominator is unchanged.
findings.assertion: For every state: the count named in the band-head label above `.kpis` equals `document.querySelectorAll('.kpis .kpi .meter').length + 1` (the lead), and where any `.kpi .na` exists neither the band-head label nor `.kpi.lead .sr` contains the word "every" or "all" unqualified. In partial specifically, the band head must not read "All five".

findings.problem: Round 2 established the rule on this surface: a state that says it is still reading may not publish the reading, and every magnitude in the skeleton was neutralised in place to honour it. The coverage footer was not. Driven at ?state=loading&motion=settled, its six entries read, in one row, in one grammar: "Tasks reading · Timeline reading · Notes reading · Read 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026 · Lab counts and ages are lab-authored · Bound workspace, owner, reading date and the 9". Three entries say the read is in progress and the fourth, immediately beside them and in the same voice, says when it completed. The reading line at the top of the page prints the same stamp a second time ("Read at 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026"), at full ink, above a page that has been emptied of every other fact. Two text nodes carry `readingLong` in this state; both are magnitudes the state does not hold.
findings.consequence: The one row on this surface whose job is to tell the owner what the instrument actually read contradicts itself while they watch. It is the same lie the neutralised skeleton was built to stop telling — the numbers were taken out and the timestamp on them was left in — and it is the entry a reader checks precisely when they are unsure whether what they are looking at is current.
findings.fix:
Make the Read entry a source like the other three. In `SOURCES.loading` add `read: "reading"`, and in `shell()` print `Read ${state === "loading" ? "reading" : esc(D.readingLong)}`. In the reading line, print `

${state === "loading" ? "Reading now" : `Read at ${esc(D.readingLong)}`}

`. Both keep their box, their rank and their place, so no geometry moves when the data lands.
findings.assertion: In state=loading at both grounds and every declared viewport: `LATELY_FIXTURE.readingLong` and `LATELY_FIXTURE.readingShort` appear in zero text nodes in the document, and `.coverage` contains no digit other than those in the lab/bound provenance entries. In every non-loading state the reading instant still appears at least once.

findings.element: the all-clear heading in ?state=quiet and the .ages card heading, both inside section[aria-labelledby=m2q]
findings.problem: "Sitting" is used exactly twice on the whole surface, both times as a `.t-head` at the same typographic rank, both inside the same section, and it means opposite things. Measured at 1440, ?state=quiet: "Nothing is sitting" at y=739, "How long open work has been sitting" at y=963 — 224px apart, no other heading between them. In the first it means "stalled past a fortnight"; in the second it means "open". Under the second heading the card then draws nine marks and prints "Oldest · 12 days". Every other place the surface names this idea it says it precisely — the KPI card says "haven't moved in a fortnight", the spoken line says "open longer than a fortnight" — so the loose word appears only where it collides with itself.
findings.consequence: The quiet state exists to let an owner stop worrying. It tells them nothing is sitting and then, a card later, shows them nine things and how long each has been sitting, the oldest for twelve days. Read cold — which is the whole audience for this product — that is the surface contradicting itself, and it costs the all-clear its authority in the one state whose entire job is to be believed.
findings.fix:
Change the all-clear heading to answer the section that contains it: `

Nothing is slipping

` (the section is titled "What's quietly slipping"). One word, no other copy moves, and "sitting" is then used once on the surface, in the ages card, with one meaning. Note that interaction-check.mjs:817 gates a whole block of assertions on `reassures: /Nothing is sitting/.test(text)` — that key must move with the copy or those checks silently stop running, which is the same class as the finding above.
findings.assertion: In state=quiet at both grounds: the all-clear `.t-head` does not contain /sitting/i, and across the whole document the token "sitting" appears in at most one heading. Plus: the gate's own conditional key at interaction-check.mjs:817 matches the shipped all-clear heading, proven by asserting that the guarded block runs (a counter incremented inside it is non-zero) in state=quiet.

findings.problem: `.center` sets `gap: var(--gap-line)` (16px) between its children. In the empty and quiet states the heading and its explanation are siblings of `.center` and take that rung — measured 16.0px in both. In the error state they are wrapped in `<div role="alert">` for the r1 fix terminal-states-lose-their-heading-and-announce-nothing, so they become one flex child and nothing sets a gap between them: measured 0.0px, on light and on dark, at 1440. The surface's stated invariant is that every gap on it is a rung on the declared ladder; 0 is not a rung, and the ladder assertion at interaction-check.mjs:625 reads margins only, so it cannot see a gap that was never declared.
findings.consequence: The error state's headline and its explanation set solid against each other, unlike the identical composition in every other centred state, so the two collapse into one block at the moment the reader is already trying to work out what went wrong. It is a small break and it is in the state least able to afford one.
findings.fix: Give the alert wrapper the rung its siblings have: `.center > [role="alert"] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--gap-line); }`. Nothing else moves; the wrapper keeps its role and its announcement.
findings.assertion: In state=error at both grounds and every declared viewport: the vertical distance between the bottom of `[role=alert] h2` and the top of `[role=alert] p` equals the computed `gap` of the enclosing `.center` (16px), and equals the same measurement taken between the heading and paragraph of the empty state.

findings.element: .note paragraph under the KPI row in ?state=partial
findings.problem: The note reads: "Timeline did not answer this reading, so nothing here knows a due date. The card keeps its place and says so; it does not fall back to zero." The first sentence is the owner's. The second is the studio's — it names a component ("the card"), describes a layout decision ("keeps its place") and defends a policy to a reviewer ("it does not fall back to zero"). r1 closed refusals-written-in-the-studio-vocabulary on the three limit tiles; the class is back, in a different element, and the paid defect library records it as raised three separate times in one previous engagement.
findings.consequence: A venue owner is handed a sentence about the product's internal policy at the moment they wanted to know whether anything is overdue. It costs a line of reading and tells them nothing they can act on, and it is the only place on this surface where the product talks about itself.
findings.fix: Cut the second sentence and, if the note needs a second beat, replace it with the owner's next fact: "Timeline did not answer this reading, so nothing here knows a due date. Everything else on this page was read normally."
findings.assertion: In state=partial: the `.note` text contains none of /the card/i, /falls? back/i, /keeps its place/i, and no reference to a class or component name on this surface; it names only the source that did not answer and what that means for the reader.

biggestWin: Bound the first-run hero card to its own content. The solo plot was narrowed to 57px in r1 and its ruler was narrowed to match in r2, but the grid track is still 1fr and the card still runs to the page edge, so 58% of the card at 1440 and 82.6% at 768 is blank paper around a single mark. That card is the first object a new venue owner ever sees on this surface, and right now it reads as a chart that failed to render rather than as a product saying, deliberately, that it holds one week of record. Carrying the same narrowing one container up — `grid-template-columns: minmax(220px,300px) auto` on the hero and `width: max-content; max-width: 100%` on the card — draws nothing new, refuses nothing less, and turns the surface's weakest first impression into a composition.
